Bringers
BRING-erz
n.
From Old English bringan (to bring, to carry), the agent noun in its plural form; appearing once in the Authorized Version, in the account of Jehu's letter to the rulers of Jezreel and Samaria.

Biblical Definition

The elders also, and the bringers up of the children, sent to Jehu.

Bringers appears once in the Authorized Version, in the phrase the bringers up of the children, naming those entrusted with the rearing and education of the seventy sons of Ahab left in Samaria after his death. Jehu, moving to exterminate Ahab's house per Elijah's prophecy against it (1Ki 21:21-22), sent a deliberately provoking letter to the rulers, elders, and bringers up of the children, daring them to set the best and meetest of their master's sons on his throne and fight for the house of their lord (2Ki 10:2-3). Terrified by Jehu's reputation and unwilling to stand against him, they instead sent back word we will do all that thou shalt bid us; we will not make any king (2Ki 10:5), and the seventy sons were beheaded the next day at Jehu's command. The bringers up of the children occupied a position of trust and responsibility Scripture takes seriously — men charged with raising the next generation of a royal house — and their answer here is a study in worldly self-preservation rather than covenant loyalty, choosing survival under a new king over any principled stand, whether for good or ill, regarding the household they had been set to raise.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828), from BRING UP: to educate, to rear from infancy; the plural agent noun here naming those charged with rearing Ahab's seventy sons in Samaria.

expand to see more

BRING UP, v.t. To rear; to educate; to instruct and form the manners of in youth.

BRINGERS, n. plural. Those who bring up or rear; guardians, tutors.

In 2 Kings 10:5 the word names those responsible for rearing Ahab's seventy royal sons.

Jehu's letter tested their loyalty to the house of Ahab against Elijah's prophesied judgment.

Their answer, 'we will not make any king,' shows survival chosen over covenant loyalty either way.

Key Scripture

2Ki 10:5 — "And he that was over the house, and he that was over the city, the elders also, and the bringers up of the children, sent to Jehu, saying, We are thy servants, and will do all that thou shalt bid us; we will not make any king: do thou that which is good in thine eyes."

Modern Corruption

A reading focused only on Jehu's severity can miss that the bringers up of the children are themselves indicted here for a cowardly self-preservation that abandons the household entrusted to their care rather than standing for anything at all.

expand to see more

The episode is sometimes read purely as commentary on Jehu's violence, but the text gives equal weight to the officials' own moral failure: charged with raising the next generation faithfully, they instead hand their charges over the moment loyalty becomes costly.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the weight Scripture places on those who raise and teach the young: the office itself is honorable, and its holders are judged by whether they exercise it faithfully when faithfulness is costly, not only when it is easy.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Bringers up occurs once, naming the guardians of Ahab's seventy sons in Samaria, whose cowardly capitulation to Jehu's threat resulted in the sons' execution and completed Elijah's prophesied judgment on Ahab's house.

expand to see more

Bringers up in 2 Kings 10:5 names the guardians charged with rearing Ahab's seventy sons.

Jehu's letter (2Ki 10:2-3) tested whether they would set a son on the throne and fight for the house.

Their reply, 'we will not make any king,' chose self-preservation over any stand at all.

The seventy sons were beheaded the next day, fulfilling Elijah's judgment on Ahab's house (1Ki 21:21-22).

The office of rearing the young is treated as a serious trust, judged by faithfulness under pressure.

Usage

"The elders also, and the bringers up of the children, sent to Jehu, saying, We are thy servants."

"We will not make any king: do thou that which is good in thine eyes (2Ki 10:5)."

"I will cut off from Ahab him that pisseth against the wall (1Ki 21:21) — the prophecy this episode fulfills."
